Beállítom Vizsgálatot indított Tena Šimonović Einwalter horvát ombudsman annak tisztázására, hogy sérthette-e a betegek jogait a spliti klinikai központ gyakorlata, amely szerint nem megfelelő öltözet esetén megtagadhatják a betegfelvételt. A kórház szerint a nyári hőségben is elvárható az egészségügyi intézményhez illő ruházat. Az ombudsman szerint egy kórház joggal szabhat bizonyos öltözködési feltételeket, például kifogásolhatja a fürdőruhát, az azonban már betegjogi kérdés, ha valakit a nadrág vagy az ingujj hossza miatt küldenek el. A horvát sajtó beszámolója szerint az egyik panaszos földig érő, széles pántos nyári ruhában próbált az egyik spliti kórházban a központi recepciós pultnál időpontot foglalni 32 éves fiának hasi ultrahangvizsgálatára. A biztonsági őr nem szólt semmit, de a pultnál dolgozó alkalmazott udvariasan közölte vele, hogy nem tartja megfelelőnek a lenge ruházatot. A nőnél szerencsére volt a táskájában váltóruha, így gyorsan átöltözött, és ezt követően már el tudta intézni a jelentkezést. Az eset után a biztonsági őr még oda is ment hozzá, elnézését kérve. Az ombudsman magyarázatot kért a spliti klinikai központtól, és azt vizsgálja, hogy az előírásokat egységesen és a betegek jogainak tiszteletben tartásával alkalmazták-e. A kórház közölte, hogy betegeitől és látogatóitól kulturált, az intézményhez illő megjelenést vár el. Álláspontja szerint a dalmáciai hőségben is lehet könnyű ruházatot viselni anélkül, hogy az fürdőruhaszerű, különösen hiányos vagy átlátszó lenne. A sürgős ellátásra az előírások nem vonatkoznak. Az ombudsman a vizsgálat lezárása után foglal állást arról, hogy a kórházi gyakorlat összhangban állt-e a betegek egészségügyi ellátáshoz fűződő jogaival. http://www.shanghainews.net/news/2793059.text: Home China News International News Business News Search News Network NATO says growing Russian threat, an ‘act of desperation’ Mohan Sinha 17 Sep 2026, 08:59 GMT+ WARSAW, Poland: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said on September 14 that Russian drone strikes near the Ukraine-Poland border would lead the military alliance to increase its support for Kyiv. He described the attacks as a sign that Russian forces were becoming increasingly desperate. "The strikes yesterday on trains in Ukraine close to NATO territory again show Putin's desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror," Rutte said at NATO headquarters in Brussels. Rutte said NATO would increase its support for Ukraine and strengthen the defenses of its 32 member countries along the alliance's eastern border with Russia. He also said Russian President Vladimir Putin would not succeed in weakening NATO's unity or stopping its support for Ukraine. Rutte's comments came after Poland announced stronger security measures along its border with Ukraine. The move followed a series of Russian drone attacks near the frontier, including two drones that came down only a few kilometers from Polish territory. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned on September 13 that Russia appeared ready to increase attacks connected to Ukraine's borders with European countries. Ukraine is already facing an intense Russian air campaign involving ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones designed to break through its air defenses. Tusk said the coming weeks and months could bring a major increase in Russian activity. He also warned that the escalation could affect Polish territory. He had issued a similar warning on September 10. Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said on X that the Polish army had recovered what appeared to be a Russian military drone from the Baltic Sea near the coastal village of Jaroslawiec. Polish officials said intelligence assessments, including information from a CIA briefing the previous week, indicated that Russia could target border areas and increase sabotage operations in European countries. The reported aim would be to discourage Western countries from continuing their support for Ukraine. Tusk said Poland would discuss preparations for a possible joint response with its NATO allies. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski highlighted NATO's military strength. He said European NATO air forces, even without U.S. involvement, would be capable of destroying half of Russia's oil refineries more quickly than Ukraine could. Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk described the latest drone attacks as a serious escalation by Russia. He said any conflict spilling into European countries could involve sabotage, a major increase in hybrid warfare or other hostile actions along NATO's borders. The developments have increased concerns among NATO members that Russia's war against Ukraine could increasingly affect neighboring European countries. Poland, which shares a border with Ukraine and lies on NATO's eastern flank, has been particularly alert to the risk of Russian attacks or other hostile activity crossing into its territory. https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/19/trum.text: US President Donald Trump left China on Thursday without meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, a get-together he had sought during his visit to Shenzhen for a rare three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.Trump had repeatedly raised the possibility of meeting Kim during his Asia trip, although a White House official had said no such meeting was planned.“We may meet with Kim Jong-un also, so that'll be good,” Trump told reporters at the White House on Monday.Meanwhile, Kim inspected sites in North Korea’s South Hamgyong province on Tuesday and Wednesday, according to South Korean news agency Newsis.The two leaders have not met face-to-face since June 2019.Although the three leaders agreed to pursue dialogue on nuclear risk reduction and non-proliferation, the joint “peace declaration” made no explicit reference to the Korean Peninsula or Taiwan.However, Chinese state news agency Xinhua later reported that the three leaders had exchanged views on the Korean Peninsula, Ukraine, nuclear non-proliferation and the situation in the Middle East.The summit has fuelled concerns in South Korea, Japan and Taiwan that major powers could make decisions affecting regional security without consulting those directly affected.South Korea fears being sidelinedBefore the three-way meeting, South Korean media compared it to the Yalta Conference in 1945, where leaders of the US, the UK and the Soviet Union discussed the post-war international order.Seoul has been keen to avoid major powers making decisions on the Korean peninsula without its involvement.Although the omission of the Korean peninsula from the declaration has somewhat alleviated concerns over a second Yalta, it has raised concerns that denuclearisation is slipping down the major powers’ diplomatic agenda, according to South Korean news outlet Money Today.Park Won-gon, a professor of North Korean studies at Ewha Womans University, told the outlet that China and Russia may have sided with Pyongyang.Kim Jae-chun, a professor at Sogang University, said the three powers view North Korea’s nuclear programme very differently.However, Newsis suggested that the absence of a Trump-Kim meeting for the second consecutive year may ease concerns over potential US recognition of North Korea as a nuclear-armed state.South Korean President Lee Jae-myung reiterated, during Thursday’s APEC summit, the importance of achieving peace and stability on the Korean peninsula to bring prosperity to the region.Japan seeks reassurances from WashingtonThe three-way meeting has raised concerns in Japan, where relations with Beijing are tense.Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi exchanged greetings with Xi during APEC, but the two leaders did not meet formally.A Japanese ruling-party lawmaker said Japan’s exclusion from the three-way meeting could be seen as a diplomatic setback, Fuji TV reported.However, Takaichi said at a press briefing in Shenzhen that she did not believe Japan’s interests would be undermined by the summit, Japanese broadcaster TBS reported.Takaichi is also arranging a phone call with Trump to discuss the outcome of his talks with Xi and Putin and reaffirm bilateral cooperation, TV Asahi reported, citing Japanese government sources.Japanese media also highlighted the three powers’ position on the International Criminal Court (ICC), which is currently headed by Japanese judge Tomoko Akane.The joint declaration called for respect for the immunity of state officials and said that the ICC and similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction.In March 2023, the court issued an arrest warrant for Putin over the alleged unlawful deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children.Taiwan wary of great-power diplomacyAs with South Korea, mentions of "Yalta 2.0" emerged in Taiwanese media in the lead-up to the meeting. Taiwanese broadcaster TVBS highlighted concerns that Taiwan could be used as a bargaining chip in the negotiations.The question of Taiwan was raised in the bilateral meeting between Xi and Trump earlier on Thursday.Tsai Jung-hsiang, a professor of political science at National Chung Cheng University in Taiwan, told the island’s Central News Agency that the US and China have very different views on strategic stability.While Trump has aimed to avoid conflict over Taiwan during his time in office, Xi wanted the US to recognise Beijing’s position on sovereignty and territorial integrity, Tsai said.However, he said he did not expect any changes to US policy regarding Taiwan as a result of the meeting.State-run media in China said the three-way meeting allowed the three major powers to work together to promote international security and stability.Xi said the meeting was “positive, constructive and fruitful”, as the three nations were committed to “world peace”, Xinhua reported.Earlier, Xi said the three nations should hold regular high-level meetings and establish mechanisms to prevent and manage crises.Neither proposal was explicitly included in the four-point peace declaration.

US President Donald Trump has “sharply questioned” European countries over their continued financial support for Ukraine during the country’s conflict with Russia.The president unexpectedly phoned into a meeting of Ukraine’s European allies on Thursday, according to the Politico publication, which heard from four European officials who were briefed on the discussion.He asked the allies why they were continuing to spend billions on military support for Kyiv.The call came mere hours after Trump wrapped up a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Chinese counterpart, President Xi Jinping, in Shenzhen, China.The US president is said to have called Berlin from his private aircraft, Air Force One, and insisted that Putin was serious about future peace negotiations about Ukraine.Three of the European officials, who have been granted anonymity, said that Trump was strongly sceptical about the possibility of further aid being provided to Ukraine by the Coalition of the Willing, an alliance of 34 countries – plus Ukraine – who have pledged strengthened support for Ukraine against Russian aggression.One of the officials said Trump bemoaned the fact that a lot of people are dying in the conflict, and a lot of money is being “wasted” on the nearly five-year-long war. That official also confirmed that the US leader believes Putin will cooperate with peace negotiations with Ukraine.This is a developing story.
